quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean away from the turn direction.
Keep the motorcycle upright while leaning your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, do the opposite. Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans into the turn.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: When you use either brake lever, both the front and rear brakes apply.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you use either brake lever, both the front and rear brakes apply.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes work at the same time. Read your owner's manual to learn about your specific braking system.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle in front. This gives you more time to notice they are stopping and to slow down or stop safely.

questions.question: Who sets the pace for a group of riders?
questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the pace. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on the motorcycle?

options.text: At the rear of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: The passenger should board only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider's control. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Put less experienced riders near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders behind them watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: When picking a helmet, what should you NOT prioritize?

options.text: Meeting U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. More experienced riders behind them can watch them.

questions.question: What does it mean when the rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Hand signals work instead of turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it signals a right turn or right lane change.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try not to place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can make it hard to control the motorcycle.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist stop other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers who try to move into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern across the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This discourages other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle and car crashes are caused by the car driver not yielding the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver fails to yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do when riding?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and seem slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge where they are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT tell a passenger before they ride?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep a large space between yourself and the rider.
Keep your legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between yourself and the rider.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on after the engine starts. They should sit forward as close as possible without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before turning.
When turning, lean in the direction you wish to go.
Avoid dragging your feet on the roadway.

questions.explanation: Slow to a safe speed before turning and lean in the direction you turn. Don't drag your feet on the road, or you could lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: Why should you not ride too far to the right on your lane if you have a sidecar or three-wheeled motorcycle?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. Riding too far right can cause it to run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: What gear should you be in when you are stopped?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What vest or jacket color helps you be seen the best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing while riding to be seen better. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green colors work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: Groups should use single-file formation when taking curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is used on straight roads.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which portion of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane before passing. This position helps you see ahead better and makes oncoming traffic more aware of you.

questions.question: Usually, a minimum following distance of _____ should be maintained.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to three seconds or more.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing vehicle is dangerous.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a turn. Close the throttle and use both brakes if needed.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. Choose a position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds below 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been previously worn in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been previously worn in an accident.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no visible damage. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to potential road hazards ahead.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Doesn't mean that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver sees you just because they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still don't notice them.
